programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
programme.sub-title: Libya - If You Break It You Own It
programme.desc: A look at Barack Obama's first presidential trip abroad to Cairo, where he addressed the younger generation in the Arab world and told them 'you, more than anyone, have the ability to remake this world'. A year and a half later the Arab Spring broke out, leaving Obama to decide whether he should heed the call to save innocent civilians from Muammar Gaddafi's threats of a potential massacre

programme.title: Treasures of Ancient Greece
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke traces the complex and fascinating story of Western civilisation's love affair with Greek art, learning how people in succeeding centuries found inspiration for their own ideals and ambitions. Filming in Britain, France, Italy and Germany, Alastair visits the Aphrodite of Knidos, which was the first naked woman in Western art; the bronze horses of St Mark's in Venice, which became a pawn in an imperial game; and the Discobolus, which was purchased by Nazi leader Adolf Hitler

programme.title: Leonardo
programme.sub-title: The Secret Life of the Mona Lisa
programme.desc: Alan Yentob tells the story of how Leonardo Da Vinci's Mona Lisa became the most famous painting in the world. Admired by six million tourists every year, surrounded by bodyguards and encased in a humidified, air-conditioned box protected by bullet-proof glass, the enigmatic masterpiece has been stolen, vandalised and exploited over the centuries. With the help of leading scholars and original research, the subject of the portrait is finally revealed - along with the reason behind her inscrutable smile

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.sub-title: Dundee to Loch of the Lowes
programme.desc: Michael Portillo's rail journey through post-war Scotland takes him over the River Tay to Dundee, Scotland's fourth largest city. He is on the trail of Joseph McKenzie, the father of modern Scottish photography. Alighting at Dunkeld, the host makes for the Loch of the Lowes, to spot a pair of breeding ospreys

programme.title: Walking with
programme.desc: Chef Monica Galetti ventures through the landscapes of the North York Moors, along the way she meets local residents and samples local produce. Monica begins in the historic village of Rosedale Abey, before following the course of a stream up Rosedale and climbing towards the heather. Crossing over to Farndale, she walks the quiet lanes and ends with a drink in the hamlet of Church Houses

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth develops a passion for art, Rose acquires a new admirer, and Daddy has a yearning to join the Foreign Legion. Patricia Routledge stars

programme.title: One Foot in the Grave
programme.desc: Victor endures a sleepless night - and naturally ensures the eternally put-upon Margaret and their neighbours share in his suffering. Comedy, starring Richard Wilson and Annette Crosbie

programme.title: She-Wolves: England's Early Queens
programme.desc: Historian Helen Castor explores the lives of Isabella of France and Margaret of Anjou, two French-born queens of England whose ambition and desire for power caused outrage in medieval Britain. Isabella, wife of King Edward II in the 14th century, was accused of murder, while 100 years later Margaret, who was married to Henry VI, was regarded as a destructively ambitious figure - and would go on to be labelled a 'she-wolf' by Shakespeare. However, Castor argues it was their gender, rather than their behaviour, that lay at the root of their public vilification

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Historian Sam Willis charts how Edward I turned the castle into an instrument of colonisation. He spent a large amount of money on subduing the Welsh and built fearsome fortresses in Caernarfon, Gwynedd and Beaumaris, which were used to impose England's rule on the country. However, when the king's attention turned to Scotland, his plans didn't go as expected

programme.title: Corridors of Power: Should America Police the World?
programme.sub-title: Darfur - Carrots for a War Criminal
programme.desc: A look at how, in 2003, the Sudanese government began a widespread ethnic cleansing campaign in the western part of the country. Hundreds of thousands of Americans went out to protest and demand protection for the citizens of Darfur. Following Obama's 2008 election success, many of the people that fought so vocally for Darfur came into office

programme.title: The Treasures of Ancient Rome
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke explores the artistic achievements of the Romans, tracing their progression from thieves and copycats to pioneers of the use of unflinching realism. Portraits from the Republic reveal how they captured lifelike images and immortalised figures such as Julius Caesar and Cicero using marble, bronze and paint. Alastair also looks at how Rome's first emperor, Augustus, used art as a tool to forge his dominion

programme.title: Caligula with Mary Beard
programme.desc: Roman emperor Gaius Julius Caesar Augustus Germanicus - better known as Caligula - was said to have made his horse a consul, proclaimed himself a living God and indulged in scandalous orgies. In this documentary, classical scholar Mary Beard attempts to peel away some of the myths surrounding him, sifting through surviving evidence to paint a portrait of the real Caligula

programme.title: Sir Derek Jacobi Remembers - I, Claudius
programme.desc: The veteran actor looks back at the landmark 1976 drama, based on the novels of Robert Graves, telling the life story of a reluctant Roman emperor

programme.title: I, Claudius
programme.desc: Acclaimed drama set amidst a web of power, corruption and lies, chronicling the reigns of the Roman emperors - Augustus, Tiberius, Caligula and finally Claudius - focusing on the intrigue that surrounded their respective reigns. Augustus's wife Livia schemes to ensure her son Tiberius succeeds her husband. The dispute between Marcus Agrippa and Marcellus reaches boiling point, prompting the former to leave Rome for the East. With Derek Jacobi, Sian Phillips, Brian Blessed and George Baker

programme.title: I, Claudius
programme.desc: Augustus refuses to forgive Tiberius, but remains blissfully unaware of Julia's philandering. Lucius is promoted to command the army in Spain following the inexplicable death of his brother

programme.title: Talking Pictures

programme.desc: Celia Imrie revisits one of cinema's greatest decades with a deeper dig into the BBC archives, uncovering revealing interviews and magic movie moments from 1970s Hollywood. Featuring a look at a teenage Linda Blair shrugging off the revulsion that had movie-goers' heads spinning with The Exorcist, and Clint Eastwood's hippy-sounding relaxation techniques at the time of Dirty Harry

programme.desc: The amateur sewers tackle the fast fashion industry in reduce, reuse and recycle week, with three challenges focused on the environment and sustainability. They then use various waste items, from baubles to bike tyres, to help decorate their transformations, before creating made-to-measure outfits with an environmental message

Facing parental pressure and everyday racism, he unexpectedly finds his frustrations and ambitions expressed in Bruce Springsteen songs. Inspired by the rock star and a teacher who encourages his own writing, he sets out to fulfill his dreams. Coming-of-age drama, starring Viveik Kalra, Kulvinder Ghir and Meera Ganatra

Comedy, starring Anna Kendrick, Brittany Snow, Anna Camp, Rebel Wilson and Skylar Astin

programme.title: Pitch Perfect 2 (2015)
programme.desc: A Cappella group the Barden Bellas enjoy an unprecedented run of success, until a disastrous performance sees them banned from national competitions and beset by scandal. They attempt to turn their fortunes around and redeem their reputation by competing in the World Championships of A Cappella in Copenhagen. Comedy sequel, starring Anna Kendrick and Rebel Wilson

programme.title: Spider-Man (2002)
programme.desc: A clumsy teenager develops superhuman powers after a genetically engineered spider bites him. At first his fantastic skills delight him, but his elation is severely tempered by a family tragedy, prompting him to dedicate his talents to combating evil. However, he faces a baptism of fire in the form of crazed villain the Green Goblin. Comic-book superhero adventure, with Tobey Maguire, Kirsten Dunst, Willem Dafoe, James Franco and Rosemary Harris

programme.title: Spider-Man 2 (2004)
programme.desc: Peter Parker continues his fight for justice, but unrequited love and personal worries take their toll and he is tempted to abandon his web-slinging alter ego. However, the arrival of deadly new bad guy Doctor Octopus plunges him into a race against time to save New York. Comic-book adventure sequel, with Tobey Maguire, Kirsten Dunst, Alfred Molina, James Franco and Rosemary Harris

programme.title: Spider-Man 3 (2007)
programme.desc: A sinister alien parasite brings out the web-slinging hero's darker side, filling him with thoughts of revenge on his uncle's murderer, the shape-shifting Sandman. Meanwhile, he also has to contend with the challenge of his best friend following in his father's villainous footsteps - and a jealous rival developing superpowers of his own. Superhero sequel, with Tobey Maguire, Kirsten Dunst and James Franco
